summary_responses.response: The Bureau of the Fiscal Service, Department of the Treasury, has issued a final rule amending 31 CFR Part 356, the Uniform Offering Circular (UOC) that sets the terms and conditions for the sale and issuance of marketable book-entry Treasury bills, notes, and bonds. Treasury also clarifies that the denominator in the index ratio formula is always the reference Consumer Price Index applicable for the original dated date, though none of the changes affect the calculation of adjusted value, index ratio, or settlement amount for inflation-protected securities. The most substantive modification requires submitters to provide each individual customer's name and bid amount for all noncompetitive bids before the noncompetitive auction close, eliminating summary bid amounts, with these changes applying beginning with the first auction conducted using Treasury's upgraded auction system. Finally, the rule removes references to treasurydirect.gov in favor of stating that auction results will be made available on Treasury's website, and Treasury determined that the rule is exempt from Administrative Procedure Act notice and comment requirements because it relates to contracts, is not a significant regulatory action under Executive Order 12866, and involves no collection of information.

summary_responses.response: This paper introduces DiffTry (Differential Retries), a lightweight, stateless mechanism that transforms retries into a rejection-prioritization control for microservice architectures, where independently auto-scaled services frequently miscoordinate and overload, causing valuable transactions to be rejected and enabling attackers to amplify damage with cheap low-value traffic. DiffTry works by assigning class-specific retry-attempt limits (e.g., three attempts for premium/high-priority requests versus one for low-priority or batch traffic) at the point where rejections occur, requiring no overload sensing, no service coordination, and no application-code changes, and remaining effectively silent under normal load. The authors develop an analytical model, beginning with a fluid-model approximation for a two-service tandem under overload and a queueing-based (M/M/1/m) treatment of the no-overload regime, then generalize it to arbitrary service networks using an open-network flow model with priority classes, deriving per-node and end-to-end rejection rates via a convergent iterative solution, proving uniqueness for DAG-structured transaction graphs, and establishing that class-level success rates increase monotonically with retry limits. Simulation results confirm the model's accuracy, and the illustrative example shows that with equal input loads from both classes, high-priority transactions achieve roughly 85% of successful completions (about a 70% throughput improvement) while their rejection rate drops to around 15%. The predictions are validated on a live Kubernetes deployment as a drop-in service-mesh plugin, where measured rejection rates closely match the analysis, confirming that the local retry-budget mechanism composes into network-wide prioritization in practice.

summary_responses.response: The Office of Personnel Management (OPM) issued a direct final rule making technical revisions to its Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) regulations in 5 CFR part 630, subpart L, to incorporate statutory amendments enacted in January 2021 and December 2023. The rule is effective December 14, 2026, unless significant adverse comments are received by November 16, 2026, in which case OPM would withdraw the affected provisions and issue a notice of proposed rulemaking. The 2021 amendments (Public Law 116-283) exclude Veterans Health Administration employees covered by a leave system under 38 U.S.C. 7421 from title 5 FMLA coverage, broaden the 12-month qualifying service requirement to include virtually all civilian Federal service (including temporary or intermittent service and Postal Service, Postal Regulatory Commission, and non-appropriated fund instrumentality service), and clarify that annual or sick leave earned under authorities outside title 5 may be substituted for unpaid FMLA leave. The December 2023 amendment (Public Law 118-31) allows honorable active military service in the Army, Navy, Air Force, Space Force, or Marine Corps to count toward the 12-month service requirement for FMLA and paid parental leave eligibility, though not Coast Guard or commissioned Public Health Service service. Because paid parental leave is substituted for unpaid FMLA leave, these changes also affect PPL eligibility, and the rule codifies guidance previously issued in OPM memoranda CPM 2021-07 and CPM 2024-05.
